title: Podcast Platform
seoTitle: Design a Podcast Platform like Apple Podcasts
description: Design a podcast platform — ingesting millions of RSS feeds, detecting new episodes efficiently, serving audio from CDNs, subscriptions and new-episode notifications, and syncing playback position.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is a Podcast Platform?
blocks.text: A podcast platform (Apple Podcasts, Pocket Casts, Spotify's podcast side) lets listeners find shows, subscribe, and play or download episodes. Unlike music, most podcasts aren't uploaded to the platform: creators publish an **RSS feed** on their own hosting, and the platform must discover new episodes by polling millions of feeds.

items: The platform should ingest podcasts from RSS feeds and pick up new episodes soon after publication.
Users should be able to search and subscribe to shows.
Subscribers should be notified of new episodes, and episodes can auto-download.
Users should be able to stream or download episodes and resume where they left off on any device.
Ads insertion and analytics for creators.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: New episodes should appear within ~15 minutes for popular shows, and within hours for inactive ones.
Be polite to creators' servers: don't hammer feeds.
Handle ~5M shows and ~100M listeners, with huge download spikes when a popular show releases.
Playback position syncs across devices within seconds.
**Show**: feed URL, title, author, artwork, last fetched, polling schedule.
**Episode**: show, GUID from the feed, title, audio URL, duration, publish date.
**Playback state**: user, episode, position, completed flag, updated at.

blocks.text: A **feed scheduler** decides when each show is due for a fetch and puts it on a queue. **Fetchers** download the RSS XML, the **parser** extracts episodes and upserts them by their feed **GUID** (so re-fetching the same feed doesn't create duplicates), and new episodes are published as events.
Shows and episodes are indexed into a search index. Subscriptions are rows of `(userId, showId)`, sharded by user.

A **notification worker** consumes new-episode events, looks up subscribers of the show (an index by show ID), and sends push notifications and auto-download signals. For a show with millions of subscribers, the fan-out is batched and spread over a few minutes.

Episode audio is served through **our CDN** (cached from the creator's host) so popular releases don't overwhelm small hosts. Clients send their playback position every ~15-30 seconds and on pause; the latest `updatedAt` wins, and other devices fetch it when the episode is opened.
1) How do we poll 5M feeds efficiently?

blocks.title: Poll every feed every few minutes

approach.text: Fetch every feed on a fixed short interval.

challenges.text: ~5M feeds × every 5 minutes is 16k requests per second, mostly for feeds that haven't changed in months, and it hammers small creators' servers.

approach.text: Schedule each feed based on how often it publishes and how many subscribers it has: daily news shows every few minutes, dormant feeds once a day. Use **conditional GETs** (`ETag`, `If-Modified-Since`) so unchanged feeds return a tiny `304`.

challenges.text: Still up to minutes of delay, and still polling.

approach.text: Support **WebSub** (PubSubHubbub) and hosting-provider webhooks: big podcast hosts notify us when a feed changes, so we fetch immediately. Polling remains as a safety net with adaptive intervals, and a publish-time **prediction** (many shows release at the same weekday and hour) tightens the schedule around expected releases.

challenges.text: Not every host supports push, so the polling path must remain robust.

blocks.text: 2) How do we survive release-day spikes?

When a top show drops an episode, millions of auto-downloads start within minutes. Serving through a **CDN** with request collapsing means the creator's host is hit once per edge; staggering auto-downloads with a small random delay (or on Wi-Fi/charging) flattens the peak further. Notification fan-out is rate-limited so push providers and our API aren't flooded at once.

Mention download analytics: creators are paid by downloads, so the platform should count downloads once per device per episode, following IAB-style rules (deduplicate by IP and user agent within 24 hours).
3) How do we sync playback position?

Writes are frequent but tiny. Store positions in a key-value store keyed by `(userId, episodeId)` with **last-write-wins** on `updatedAt` from the client clock, plus a server timestamp to break ties. Clients batch updates and flush on pause, background and app close, so data use stays small.

quiz.question: How do most podcasts reach the platform?
options: The platform polls the creator's RSS feed
quiz.explanation: RSS is the open distribution format for podcasts.

quiz.question: What keeps feed polling cheap?
options: Adaptive schedules and conditional GETs that return 304 when unchanged
quiz.explanation: Most feeds rarely change, so most fetches cost almost nothing.

quiz.question: How do we avoid duplicate episodes when re-fetching a feed?
quiz.explanation: The GUID uniquely identifies each item in the feed.

quiz.question: Why serve popular episodes through our CDN?
options: So release spikes don't overwhelm creators' hosting
quiz.explanation: The CDN fetches once per edge and serves millions.
